official_scoring_enabled_note: ENABLED 2026-08-13 (operator go-live, docs/qwen-mtp-go-live-runbook.md). Flipped together with reference_baseline.publication_allowed on the trusted ref qwen36-mtp-track, which is this track's PERMANENT base branch (branch-targeted by operator design decision 2026-08-13; no merge to main is planned, and the ranked workflow's qwen36-mtp-track ref allowlist arm is permanent rather than temporary). Everything this fixture pins was measured on box 3 against the real Qwen 3.6 27B tower with the pinned native MTP head (tip 6a3bee9): the 8-entry timed_prompt_pool below carries per-entry digests and MEASURED no-op references, and token_fidelity_gate_status is implemented. The precondition that previously held this false -- the pool objects and the hidden MTP correctness golden existing only on box 3 -- is SATISFIED: all 8 pool objects, the hidden MTP correctness golden and the reused serial correctness/GPQA goldens are uploaded to R2 and were re-verified by digest on download in the gates-only dispatch at tip 7b68828.
timed_prompt_pool_note: Contract layer L6 (anti-lottery). Each entry IS a timed MTP reference-rows golden (the object the ranked job downloads and passes to mtp-timed --golden), NOT the prose prompt it was seeded from. Each was generated on box 3 with `mtp-verify --emitted <plan> --generate 513` over the transformed weights tree plus the pinned MTP head, from a DIFFERENT 512-token prose seed (8 distinct domains), and each returned reference_self_consistent=true with 513 rows.
noop_decode_speedup_note: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-13 on box 3 as N-PAIR MEANS; supersedes the single-shot values measured at tip 6a3bee9. Per entry: raw_ratio = mean(depth-0 serial parent_measured_seconds_per_token over accepted pairs) / mean(depth-2 parent measured_seconds_per_token over the same pairs) -- ratio-of-means, matching how the ranked job aggregates -- over the same 512-token window and the same rows golden, candidate = a clone of the pinned baseline tree (baseline-equivalent, so each entry's honest value IS its no-op reference). noop_decode_speedup_pairs records the accepted pairs behind each mean and noop_decode_speedup_spread_pct the measured spread, so the tolerance provenance is data rather than folklore. SPREAD METHOD: conservative propagation sqrt(CV_serial^2 + CV_mtp^2) of the two legs' per-phase CVs, applied identically to every entry. It OVER-states true paired spread by roughly 1.4-1.9x because the two legs of a pair share a thermal session and are positively correlated; where exact pair-level ratios were available (beagle, botany, drama) they were 0.104%, 0.281% and 0.116%. WHY THE RE-MEASUREMENT WAS NEEDED: the 6a3bee9-era references were each ONE pair (one depth-0 run, one depth-2 run, no averaging), and they were taken in a measurably different thermal/frequency regime -- their depth-0 serial legs cluster at 0.035653 s/tok while the current regime, and the pinned on-box serial calibration 0.037994794617407023, both sit at ~0.03800 s/tok, a +6.58% delta. That delta very nearly cancels in a ratio, but not exactly and not equally per prompt, so the old references and the pinned calibration were never mutually consistent. These means put both on the same footing for the first time. OBSERVED SHIFT: predominantly upward but NOT coherent -- 6 of 8 entries moved up, essays -0.475% and medicine -0.642% moved down; mean +0.32%, range -0.64% to +1.55%. A uniform shift would pass straight through the median-of-8 statistic, so the non-uniformity is the reason per-entry re-measurement was required rather than a single global correction. REJECTION-RATE FINDING (operator-ratified 2026-08-13): timing tolerance on this track is derived from measured per-prompt spread, never inherited from the serial era, because speculative decode is structurally prompt-sensitive -- rejection-heavy prompts do more rollback and re-forward work. In THIS data the correlation between acceptance rate and CURRENT spread is weak (r = -0.26, n=8, not significant); the strong relationship is between acceptance rate and the ERROR IN THE OLD SINGLE-SHOT REFERENCE (r = -0.75): the lowest-acceptance prompts are exactly where one-pair references were least reliable (botany 0.383 -> +1.55%, plutarch 0.434 -> +1.40%, against medicine 0.585 -> -0.64% and essays 0.563 -> -0.48%). Pair-averaging has already absorbed it: current spreads are 0.14-0.44% across the pool with no acceptance ordering. TOKEN EXACTNESS IS UNAFFECTED by anything in this note -- these are timing/score tolerances only. One anomaly is on record: medicine's first 4-pair session contained a single depth-0 serial reading of 0.039470826 s/tok, a >10 sigma excursion against the 31 other accepted serial observations (the depth-0 leg does prompt-independent work, so all serial readings are interchangeable and sit at ~0.03800). Rather than discard an accepted measurement, medicine was re-run at 8 pairs: the outlier did not recur, serial CV fell 1.632% -> 0.144%, and the mean landed at 1.0845 (pooling all 12 pairs minus the outlier gives 1.0844). The 8-pair value is the one pinned here.

target.manifest_sha256_note: SHA-256 of the checked-in manifest file itself, so a tampered manifest is caught before any weight byte is read.
target.expected_source_bytes_note: Sum of the 16 pinned entries in fixtures/reference_qwen3_6_27b_4bit.sha256, which pins every file of the upstream revision including .gitattributes.
target.model_type_note: The TRANSFORMED runtime tree declares qwen3_5_text and loads as Qwen35TextModel with the `language_model.` text-tower prefix stripped; the raw pinned reference declares qwen3_5 and loads as the Qwen35Model wrapper. Both are MTP-capable and both are accepted by the worker (verified on box 3 at this tip: layout=textModel and layout=wrappedTextModel both reach the protocol hello).

mtp_head.tensor_count_note: Pinned in MLXFastConstants.qwenMTPHeadTensorCount and asserted at load: a head tree that lost or gained a tensor fails the load instead of drafting from a partly-uninitialised head.
mtp_head.merge_note: The head is a SEPARATELY PINNED tree, merged at load under the `mtp.` key prefix before sanitize and before the quantization walk. It is resident on BOTH sides of the pair, so its residency cost is charged to the serial denominator too; only the drafting differs.
mtp_head.residency_verified: Byte-verified on box 3 against fixtures/qwen3_6_27b_mtp_head.sha256: 8/8 files match sha256 and byte count, and the staging directory contains exactly those 8 files. The 8th is .gitattributes (34448b82c17d60fec9b65b1f093c115ddbaadc04beb1b0140b6bfed2e012a930, 1570 B), a genuine file of the pinned upstream revision that the original 7-record manifest omitted; it is now pinned rather than deleted from the cache.

protocol.name: trusted_qwen_mtp_block_v1
protocol.serial_control_depth_note: 0 means MTP OFF: one token per target forward, no draft, no head cache, no head forward, no verify window, no rollback. It is NOT 1. Depth 1 still drafts one token and accepts ~70% of those drafts (measured 0.699 on box 3), so dividing by depth 1 measures depth 2 against one-deep speculation rather than against serial decode, and understates the gain. The depth-0 leg is asserted structurally, not assumed: round_count == decode tokens, accepted == rejected == 0, declared == target_tail == decode tokens, is_serial_control true, uses_native_mtp_head false.

reference_baseline._note: The paired depth-0 serial control, the per-prompt no-op references and the thermal/telemetry envelope were all measured on box 3 at tip 6a3bee9. publication_allowed was flipped to true on 2026-08-13 by the operator's go-live runbook (docs/qwen-mtp-go-live-runbook.md step D); it gates ranked scoring together with official_scoring_enabled, and both are now true. The installed and calibrated on-box baseline tree is e86655528c2abe534aa2e61a454565237801aa2d, pinned by path (/opt/bench-runner/baseline/qwen3.6-27b-mtp-v1/current) and by the signed section-9d manifest rather than by any workflow commit variable.

scoring_semantics.prompt_selection: one prompt per collection; each of the 8 timed_prompt_pool collections is a singleton today, so a ranked run times ALL 8. There is no per-run draw.
scoring_semantics.per_prompt_score: raw_p = mean(serial seconds/token over p's accepted pairs) / mean(candidate seconds/token over p's accepted pairs); norm_p = raw_p / p.noop_decode_speedup
scoring_semantics.median_rule_note: 8 is EVEN, so the rule matters: the score is the mean of the two central order statistics, NOT the lower-median rule used by the per-pair mtp_decode_speedup_median diagnostic and by the CLI's own p50 fields. results.json names both.
scoring_semantics.reference_key: timed_prompt_pool[].sha256, matched against the SHA-256 of the golden object itself. Keying on the bytes rather than on argv order or a filename means an unpinned golden, or a pool re-pinned without its objects, fails closed instead of scoring against the wrong reference.
scoring_semantics.pairs_per_prompt_note: PER PROMPT, not per run: a ranked run is 8 prompts x 1 pair = 8 pairs / 16 timed phases. k=1 is the ranked default and is raisable via the wrapper's --pairs-per-prompt. The old 3/4 budget bought pair-averaging on a SINGLE prompt; the median over 8 prompts does that job and also cancels the prompt lottery, which pair-averaging on one prompt never could.
scoring_semantics.serial_denominator_banding: POOLED across prompts: the band check runs on the mean of every accepted serial pair of every prompt against the one top-level calibration. The serial control is depth 0 -- 512 plain forwards -- and is prompt-invariant by construction, since the measured pool spread lives entirely in the acceptance rate, which only the numerator sees. Pooling 8+ pairs is a stronger test than the 4-pair band it replaces; per-prompt serial means stay in the sealed breakdown so a denominator that began to move with the prompt would be visible.
scoring_semantics.rationale: Per-prompt normalisation cancels the BASELINE's prompt-dependence -- each entry's own measured no-op maps to 1.0 by construction -- but it cannot cancel the CANDIDATE's prompt-dependent improvement profile: a change that helps `medicine` and not `drama` still scores differently depending on which prompt was drawn. Single-draw scoring is therefore a prompt lottery even after normalisation. Median-of-8 cancels it by construction, and being a median rather than a mean it also de-fangs any residual error in a single prompt's pinned reference.
scoring_semantics.token_exactness: unchanged: every timed phase must return all_tokens_matched=true, parity_all_ok is the AND over every accepted pair of every prompt, and the per-prompt breakdown carries its own parity_ok so a failure names the prompt.
scoring_semantics.supersedes: the single-sampled-prompt scoring described in proposed_scoring.normalized_scoring below, which drew one pool prompt uniformly at random per run.

proposed_scoring.score: qwen_mtp_decode_speedup = (paired_serial_decode_sec_per_token at --mtp-depth 0) / (candidate decode_sec_per_token at --mtp-depth 2), over the same rows golden and the same parent-counted 512-token window
proposed_scoring.aggregation: ratio_of_means WITHIN a prompt: mean(serial seconds/token across that prompt's accepted pairs) / mean(candidate seconds/token across the same pairs). The RUN's published score is the median of the per-prompt normalised values -- see the scoring_semantics block above, which is the authority.
proposed_scoring.denominator_authority: trusted parent wall time divided by the parent-configured decode token count; worker-reported timing is never scored

normalized_scoring.status: SUPERSEDED_2026-08-13 by the top-level scoring_semantics block; retained as the record of why normalisation exists
normalized_scoring.rationale: The measured no-op reference spans 0.756 to 1.0915 across the pool. Under the ORIGINAL single-draw design one pool prompt was drawn uniformly at random per run, and without normalisation that draw would have dominated the score. Normalisation is still applied per prompt for exactly this reason; what changed is that a run now times ALL 8 prompts and publishes the median, because normalisation alone cannot cancel a candidate's own prompt-dependent improvement profile.
normalized_scoring.reference_source: timed_prompt_pool[].noop_decode_speedup, keyed by sha256. Each entry's own measured no-op normalises to 1.0.
normalized_scoring.published_score: score = median over prompts of the per-prompt normalised ratio-of-means; metrics carry the pooled raw ratio, the per-prompt breakdown and the median

proposed_scoring.token_fidelity_gate: Every emitted token must equal the serial trajectory: mtp-verify at the candidate depth must return all_tokens_matched=true AND parity_all_ok=true, with the row ledger CLOSED (reference_checked_row_total == declared_rows_total, and accepted + rejected + target_tail == declared_rows_total). Verified on box 3 across all 8 pool prompts and the hidden correctness golden.
proposed_scoring.stall_guardrail: a run whose max block latency exceeds 4x its p50 block latency is rejected. CALIBRATION NOTE: as measured, max_block_request_seconds is the FIRST block after the seed prefill and is a one-time warmup, not a stall -- it is flat to within 1% across 8/32/128/512-round windows (serial ~0.19s, depth-2 ~0.267s). At the 512 window the serial leg therefore trips 4x (measured 5.72-5.90x) while the depth-2 leg does not (3.30-3.36x). The guardrail should exclude the first block before this track is enabled.
proposed_scoring.prefill_component: none; seed prefill is charged inside the decode measurement, identically on both legs
proposed_scoring.leaderboard: separate qwen3.6-27b-mtp-v1 namespace, never mixed with the serial or DFlash tracks
proposed_scoring.measurement_protocol: minimum three accepted thermal-gated pairs per session (target four), alternating order
